short: An anti-foreign uprising that ended with eight foreign armies occupying Peking.
full:
The Yihequan, the Righteous and Harmonious Fists, grew out of martial arts and spirit-possession societies in drought-stricken Shandong in 1899. Its members turned on Chinese Christian converts and foreign missionaries and tore up the railway and telegraph lines that were reordering the countryside, believing ritual made them proof against bullets. As they moved north into Zhili the court argued over whether to suppress them or use them. On 21 June 1900 the Empress Dowager Cixi chose the second course and declared war on the powers.

Boxers and imperial troops besieged the legation quarter in Peking for fifty-five days, from 20 June until 14 August, when a relief column of the Eight-Nation Alliance, Japanese, Russian, British, French, American, German, Italian and Austro-Hungarian, fought its way in and sacked the city. Cixi fled to Xi'an in disguise. Perhaps 100,000 people died, most of them Chinese. The Boxer Protocol of 7 September 1901 demanded the execution of officials, permanent foreign garrisons along the road to the sea, and an indemnity of 450 million taels of silver payable over thirty-nine years, more than the annual revenue of the state.
